sample.description: (N, D) array, or (N, D) array_like The data to be histogrammed.

bins.description: sequence or int, optional The bin specification:

range.description: sequence, optional A sequence of length D, each an optional (lower, upper) tuple giving the outer bin edges to be used if the edges are not given explicitly in `bins`. An entry of None in the sequence results in the minimum and maximum values being used for the corresponding dimension. The default, None, is equivalent to passing a tuple of D None values.

density.description: bool, optional If False, the default, returns the number of samples in each bin. If True, returns the probability *density* function at the bin, ``bin_count / sample_count / bin_volume``.

weights.description: (N,) array_like, optional An array of values `w_i` weighing each sample `(x_i, y_i, z_i, ...)`. Weights are normalized to 1 if density is True. If density is False, the values of the returned histogram are equal to the sum of the weights belonging to the samples falling into each bin.
constraints: weights must be one of w_i

output.description: ------- ndarray The multidimensional histogram of sample x. See density and weights for the different possible semantics. edges : tuple of ndarrays A tuple of D arrays describing the bin edges for each dimension.
